section_summary: This section traces agreements and correspondence about supplying raw cotton to Japan, selling Japanese cotton textiles, and repaying the Commodity Credit Corporation. It also covers Egyptian and Indian cotton procurement, a 1948 survey of Asian cotton markets, and competing methods of financing cotton purchases in 1949.

subfiles.title: Memorandum recommending action on revised Japanese cotton agreement, concluding page
subfiles.about: Recommends a letter to Agriculture and information copies to War and the U.S. Commercial Company.
subfiles.summary: Concluding recommendations, concurrences, and attachment list for the revised cotton agreement.

subfiles.title: Revised Agreement for Purchase of U.S. Cotton for Japan
subfiles.to: Under Secretary and Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests signatures on a revised cotton agreement and a letter preserving discussion of sterling textile sales.
subfiles.summary: Explains Agriculture's proposed revision, the British sterling proposal, consultation before CCC purchases above 150,000 bales, and circulation of the response.

subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary Anderson on revised cotton agreement
subfiles.about: Responds to the revised cotton agreement and encloses a British Treasury Delegation letter.
subfiles.summary: The OCR preserves the addressee, signature, and enclosure but little of the letter's body.

subfiles.title: Letter seeking clarification of cotton preference reports
subfiles.about: Asks whether senators correctly understood the War Department's position on a preference for American cotton in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports Indian concern about press accounts suggesting American cotton would receive preference and seeks clarification for responses to India and Egypt.

subfiles.title: Letter clarifying the July 14 cotton agreement response
subfiles.about: Clarifies State's understanding of possible sterling or other currency sales under the cotton agreement.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR is sparse; the subsequent CCC letter quotes this clarification.

subfiles.title: Agriculture response rejecting sterling sales modification
subfiles.from: E. Judd, Acting Secretary of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Rejects a proposed modification allowing repayment for Japanese textiles sold for sterling.
subfiles.summary: Agriculture insists on dollar payment to protect CCC resources and avoid delay.

subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary Patterson on sterling textile sales
subfiles.about: Addresses the British proposal concerning sterling sales of Japanese cotton textiles.
subfiles.summary: Only the greeting and signature are legible; other documents identify its subject.

subfiles.title: Original cotton supply agreement excerpts
subfiles.to: Secretaries of State and War; Chairman, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Sets terms for CCC cotton shipments to Japan and repayment from textile sales.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt requires delivery of at least 60 percent of textiles for sale, dollar repayment to CCC, and approvals for credit sales. State, War, and USCC accepted it in February 1946.

subfiles.title: United Kingdom Treasury Delegation letter to Martin
subfiles.about: Discusses the British proposal for sterling trade involving Japanese cotton textiles.
subfiles.summary: The OCR is largely illegible; the addressee and date remain visible.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on revised cotton agreement
subfiles.about: Recommends action on the July 1947 cotton agreement and lists clearances and attachments.
subfiles.summary: Poor OCR preserves a recommendation and references to the July 1 agreement.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Egyptian cotton sales to Japan
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests details of anticipated Egyptian cotton purchases by Japan.
subfiles.summary: Asks about quantity, buyer, sales channels, and payment terms.

subfiles.title: Reply to Reinhart Cotton on Egyptian cotton
subfiles.about: Answers Reinhart Cotton's inquiry about Egyptian cotton procurement for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Says the Japanese government will buy, projected volume may be below 18,000 bales, and Egyptian negotiations with SCAP are underway.

subfiles.title: CCC letter proceeding under the amended cotton agreement
subfiles.from: C. C. Farrington, Commodity Credit Corporation
subfiles.about: Confirms CCC will buy cotton under the February 1946 agreement as amended in July 1947.
subfiles.summary: Relies on State's clarification that future consideration of British sterling sales remains possible.

subfiles.title: McFadden cover letter forwarding July 24 request
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of an earlier request apparently not received.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the firm's July 24 letter.

subfiles.title: Request to reopen cotton office in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests permission to send a representative to reopen the firm's Osaka cotton office.
subfiles.summary: Cites prewar trading experience and urgent Japanese mill demand for raw cotton.

subfiles.title: Conversation on Egyptian cotton for Japan
subfiles.about: Records discussion of U.S., Indian, and Egyptian cotton supplies for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Montgomery reports no U.S. commitment to supply a fixed amount after October 31.

subfiles.title: Cotton procurement allocations for Japan
subfiles.about: Provides agreed, permissive cotton procurement quantities through October 31, 1947.
subfiles.summary: Lists 350,000 U.S., 140,000 Indian, and 7,500 Egyptian bales, with no later commitment.

subfiles.title: Approval of additional CCC cotton purchases
subfiles.about: Approves CCC purchase of another 100,000 bales for Japan after consultation with War.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes additional September and October purchases for immediate shipment.

subfiles.title: Request to enlarge cotton procurement program
subfiles.about: Addresses delayed arrangements for private cotton shippers and further CCC procurement for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests an enlarged CCC program to cover the unexpected delay.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for Steelman on Japanese cotton contract
subfiles.about: Raises a contract provision affecting blending of CCC cotton with synthetic fibers.
subfiles.summary: Seeks review of the proposed restriction on Japanese textile manufacture.

subfiles.title: Steelman reply on synthetic fiber clause
subfiles.about: Agrees that occupation policy on synthetic fibers should not be decided in the cotton contract.
subfiles.summary: Notes SCAP does not plan such blending during the agreement and directs any broader issue through established occupation policy procedures.

subfiles.title: Agriculture transmittal of revised Japanese cotton contract
subfiles.about: Transmits a revised contract removing USCC as a party.
subfiles.summary: Requests signatures and distribution of signed copies.

subfiles.title: Recommendation to sign revised cotton contract
subfiles.about: Recommends concurrence in the contract transferring USCC duties to SCAP and CCC.
subfiles.summary: Explains that the contract winds down existing CCC debt and finances no new purchases.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of signed cotton contract copy
subfiles.to: E. D. White and USCC representative
subfiles.about: Sends a copy of the cotton contract signed by Secretary Marshall.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Marshall's signed contract copy.

subfiles.title: Revised Japanese cotton agreement
subfiles.from: Secretary of Agriculture and Chairman, Commodity Credit Corporation
subfiles.to: Secretaries of State and Army; Chairman, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.about: Replaces the 1946 agreement and assigns textile sales and repayment duties as USCC withdraws.
subfiles.summary: The agreement covers previously purchased CCC cotton, creates an interest-bearing receivable, and protects CCC's claim on cotton and textiles. SCAP takes charge of manufacture, sales, accounting, insurance, and a dollar trust account; credit or non-dollar sales require safeguards. It also governs USCC's transfer of outstanding contracts and terminates after USCC and CCC are paid.

subfiles.title: Understanding on cotton still unshipped from the United States
subfiles.from: Agriculture, USCC, and Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Sets procedures for cotton purchased under the old agreement but not yet shipped to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requires shipment by January 15, 1948 unless extended, assigns residual shipping duties, and addresses CCC costs.

subfiles.title: Copy of recommendation to sign revised cotton contract
subfiles.about: Repeats the recommendation to sign the revised contract removing USCC.
subfiles.summary: Copy of the memorandum on page 107.

subfiles.title: Routing note to Lewis
subfiles.about: Routes the cotton contract papers for action.
subfiles.summary: Directs Lewis to take necessary action.

subfiles.title: Cotton contract routing sheet
subfiles.to: Saltzman, Visner, Claxton, Hulick, and Conger
subfiles.about: Routes the contract file among State Department officials.
subfiles.summary: Lists recipients and action or filing instructions.

subfiles.title: Assignment of Dr. Ide P. Trotter
subfiles.to: American diplomatic officers in Nanjing, Tokyo, New Delhi, and Karachi
subfiles.about: Announces Trotter's cotton marketing survey in Japan, China, India, and Pakistan.
subfiles.summary: Instructs missions to guide his official contacts during the survey.

subfiles.title: Request for Trotter's Japan cotton report
subfiles.to: Ide P. Trotter, care of O. L. Dawson, Shanghai
subfiles.about: Requests findings on Japanese cotton before industry committee meetings.
subfiles.summary: Asks for a mailed report or urgent airgram and cable summary.

subfiles.title: Trotter's preliminary assessment of Japanese cotton needs
subfiles.about: Recommends steady raw cotton supply for Japan's existing spindles.
subfiles.summary: Warns stocks cover less than two months and defers expansion recommendations until further study.

subfiles.title: Travel authorization query for Trotter
subfiles.about: Requests authorization if Trotter is to study cotton in Greece.
subfiles.summary: Asks for a travel authorization by wire.

subfiles.title: Army message on fiscal 1949 cotton procurement
subfiles.about: Reports procurement action for American cotton under the second half of fiscal 1949 allocation.
subfiles.summary: Promises purchase and shipping updates as bids become known.

subfiles.title: Documents for diverted ECA cotton
subfiles.about: Sends negotiable documents for ECA cotton diverted to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Directs release of documented cotton for storage at Kobe.

subfiles.title: Offer of remaining ECA cotton stocks
subfiles.about: Offers 3,900 remaining bales of raw cotton to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Requests an immediate best offer or the cotton will be placed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Manila inquiry about Japanese cotton goods
subfiles.about: Requests information on alleged U.S. transshipment of Japanese cotton goods to the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Cites an Associated Press story in the Manila Chronicle.

subfiles.title: Reply to Manila on Japanese cotton goods
subfiles.from: Department of State, conveying Department of Commerce information
subfiles.about: Explains how processed Japanese cotton goods and transit shipments appear in U.S. trade.
subfiles.summary: Says some processing and transit occur, but significant shipments to the Philippines are unlikely.

subfiles.title: SCAP proposal for financing raw cotton
subfiles.about: Compares OJEIRF financing with Public Law 820 for cotton purchases.
subfiles.summary: SCAP favors OJEIRF 60-day notes pending GARIOA coordination, estimating lower cost and simpler handling. It leaves open cheaper cash methods once reimbursement procedures are certain.

subfiles.title: State memorandum on SCAP cotton financing
subfiles.about: Reviews an Army draft cable advocating Public Law 820 instead of OJEIRF.
subfiles.summary: Raises congressional intent and Far Eastern Commission concerns, while leaving financing responsibility primarily with the Army.

subfiles.title: Draft Army cable on financing Japanese cotton purchases
subfiles.about: Urges reconsideration of OJEIRF financing in favor of Public Law 820 and other funding sources.
subfiles.summary: The draft challenges SCAP's cost and timing estimates, argues Public Law 820 could save money for short term cotton purchases, and proposes a priority order for future financing. It also recommends broader bank participation and asks SCAP for comment.
